subject: Climate & Environment
title: Vehicle Emissions
description: A quick, practical guide to Vehicle Emissions.

hook.text: A typical car releases about 4.6 metric tons of CO₂ per year just from driving.

buildup.text: Tailpipes also emit NO₂, particulates, and volatile organic compounds at street level.

discovery.text: People living within 100 meters of a busy road face significantly higher health risks.

twist.text: Diesel vehicles produce less CO₂ but far more NO₂ and soot than gasoline engines.

climax.text: Electric vehicles eliminate tailpipe emissions entirely — though tire and brake dust remain.

punchline.text: Every tailpipe is a tiny smokestack at breathing height.

quiz.question: How much CO₂ does a typical car produce per year?

details.summary: Road vehicles emit nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, volatile organic compounds, and fine particulate matter from exhaust pipes, brakes, and tires. Transport accounts for roughly a quarter of global CO2 emissions and is the primary source of urban air pollution.
details.whyItMatters: Billions of people breathe polluted air along roadways daily. Vehicle emission standards and electrification are among the most direct levers for improving urban air quality.
takeaways: Diesel vehicles produce far more NOx and soot than gasoline cars
Brake and tire wear release fine particles even from electric vehicles
Emission standards have cut per-vehicle pollution by over 90 percent since the 1970s

faq.question: Do electric vehicles produce any air pollution at all?
faq.answer: Electric vehicles produce no tailpipe emissions, but brake dust, tire wear, and road surface abrasion still release fine particulate matter. Electricity generation for charging may also cause upstream pollution depending on the grid mix.

faq.question: Why did the Volkswagen diesel scandal matter for air quality?
faq.answer: VW programmed millions of diesel cars to cheat emissions tests while emitting up to 40 times the legal NOx limit during real driving. The scandal exposed gaps in testing and led to stricter real-world driving emission standards in Europe.
